analytic.equation: delta_p = 128 mu L Q / (pi D^4); u_peak = 2 u_mean (Hagen-Poiseuille)

diagnostics.cross_check_pressure_driven: Independent control: the SAME S1->S2->S3 chain re-run pressure-driven (inlet fixedValue p = analytic delta_p, outlet p = 0) on this tube geometry yields Q within ~0.02 percent of the analytic 2.5e-4 m3/s (Hagen-Poiseuille inverse). This isolates the chain as correct and attributes the flow-driven short-tube delta_p bias to the entrance region, not to S1/S2/S3.
diagnostics.flow_driven_short_tube_note: delta_p_rel_error decreases with refinement (0.77 -> 0.36) but stays far above the tolerance bands on the default S1 mesh (addLayers off). Two compounding causes, both properties of the setup rather than of the solver chain: (1) the default castellated+snap mesh is too coarse across the 4 mm diameter (mid-tube dp/dz reaches only ~49 percent of theory on the coarse mesh and ~81 percent on the fine mesh); (2) a parabolic velocity inlet with a zeroGradient pressure inlet still needs a numerical entrance length (a few tube diameters) for the pressure field to develop, and for L/D = 10.0 that region is a non-negligible fraction of the tube. Per spec 7.4 the verdict is left as fail and the tolerances are NOT widened; wall layers + a finer cross-section would be needed to bring this configuration into band.

inlet_profile: area-normalized parabolic fixedValue imposed after meshing (developed profile; no entrance-length approximation)

physics.note: laminar solver at Re 5276 validates the chain against the laminar analytic solution; not a physical-regime claim
